pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded rows are done=0 and the CHECK rejects 2. Migration 0002 has DEFAULT 0.
test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only the open items, in order.
test 'AC-3' checks only done items are listed, marked ✓, in id order (marked 3 then 1).
test 'AC-4' checks all items are listed in order, with ✓ on the done one only.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values; code uses Object.hasOwn.

The code looks correct. But the last commit dba1bbb ('Follow-up edits') removed 'AC-7:' from the test title in test/done.test.js. No test now names AC-7, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'.
test 'AC-8' checks traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all. The traffic worker passes the path with its query to fetch.

findings.what: Commit dba1bbb ('Follow-up edits', by github-actions[bot]) renamed the AC-7 test to drop its 'AC-7' id. No test names AC-7 now, so the item is unmet under the naming rule. The rename also contradicts the PR's claim that the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' at the start of the test title 'an empty table says so in every view; an empty view has its own message'.

findings.what: The unreferenced bot commit ('Follow-up edits') has no stated reason and the PR says nothing about it. The PR also says 'Changed after the go: nothing'.
findings.fix: Revert dba1bbb, or explain it in the PR.

findings.what: The README describes the views but not that other view values answer 400, or the new query-string support in traffic routes.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the 400 for unknown views.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: the list opens on open items and the view is a query parameter.
AC-7 is unnamed by any test after the last commit. All six rows of the State table have tests. The spec was not edited after the go.
I did not run the tests; CI runs them. The tests assert real behaviour. The traffic test fake and the traffic-config tests were extended, not loosened. AC-7's test lost its id.
README updated for the views; it omits the 400 behaviour.
No defects found. Object.hasOwn guards __proto__. The empty-table fallback is correct.
The view value is whitelisted and the SQL fragments are constants. Titles are HTML-escaped. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI files. The page is server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and I judged it only as behaviour.
No browser flow is available. The behaviour is covered by the HTTP-level tests.
The claim 'test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8' is untrue for AC-7 by name. The unmentioned bot commit contradicts 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The title is under 72 characters.
